name: Casco Historico (Cathedral Quarter)
tagline: The UNESCO heart around the cathedral
description: The medieval core wraps around the vast Gothic cathedral in a maze of narrow, steep lanes. It is the most atmospheric and tourist-heavy part of Toledo, packed with monuments, craft shops, marzipan sellers and history at every turn.
bestFor: Culture lovers who want landmarks, atmosphere and monuments right on the doorstep

name: Juderia (Old Jewish Quarter)
tagline: Quiet lanes of the old Jewish quarter
description: Toledo's historic Jewish quarter sits on the western side of the old town, home to the Santa Maria la Blanca and El Transito synagogues and El Greco associations. Its tighter, quieter lanes feel more intimate than the cathedral core.
bestFor: Those wanting old-town charm with a calmer, more contemplative daily feel

name: Zocodover and the Alcazar
tagline: Central square below the hilltop fortress
description: Zocodover is Toledo's main square and social hub, sitting just below the towering Alcazar fortress. This is the practical centre for buses, cafes and meeting points, busy by day and pleasantly lively into the evening around its bars.
bestFor: People who want a central base with cafes, transport and evening buzz nearby
pros: Central and well connected by bus
Plenty of cafes and tapas bars
Close to the Alcazar and museums
cons: Can be noisy at peak times

name: Santa Barbara and Beyond the Walls
tagline: Newer districts outside the medieval walls
description: Outside the walled hill, districts such as Santa Barbara offer everyday Toledo life with flatter streets, modern flats, supermarkets and better broadband. It trades historic drama for practicality, space and lower rents, while the old town stays a short walk or bus away.
bestFor: Long-stay remote workers wanting value, easier walking and reliable connections
cons: A walk or bus from the sights
